passages.text: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my insight, that you may maintain discretion and your lips may preserve knowledge.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
The father has wisdom.
The father has insight.
The father tells his son to listen carefully.
He says, “Pay attention to my wisdom.”
He says, “Incline your ear to my insight.”
He wants his son to keep discretion.
He wants his son’s lips to preserve knowledge.
passages.original: בְּ֭נִי לְחָכְמָתִ֣י הַקְשִׁ֑יבָה לִ֝תְבוּנָתִ֗י הַט־ אָזְנֶֽךָ׃ לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְזִמּ֑וֹת וְ֝דַ֗עַת שְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Though the lips of the forbidden woman drip honey and her speech is smoother than oil, in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.
passages.sermon:
A forbidden woman speaks with sweet words.
Her lips drip honey.
Her speech is smoother than oil.
But her end is bitter like wormwood.
She is sharp like a double-edged sword.
passages.original: כִּ֤י נֹ֣פֶת תִּ֭טֹּפְנָה שִׂפְתֵ֣י זָרָ֑ה וְחָלָ֖ק מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן חִכָּֽהּ׃ וְֽ֭אַחֲרִיתָהּ מָרָ֣ה כַֽלַּעֲנָ֑ה חַ֝דָּ֗ה כְּחֶ֣רֶב פִּיּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to Sheol.
passages.sermon:
The forbidden woman is dangerous.
Her feet go down to death.
Her steps lead straight to Sheol.
Sheol means the place of the dead.
She leads people toward destruction.
passages.original: רַ֭גְלֶיהָ יֹרְד֣וֹת מָ֑וֶת שְׁ֝א֗וֹל צְעָדֶ֥יהָ יִתְמֹֽכוּ׃

passages.text: She does not consider the path of life; she does not know that her ways are unstable.
passages.sermon: The forbidden woman does not think about the path of life.\r\nShe does not know that her ways are unstable.
passages.original: אֹ֣רַח חַ֭יִּים פֶּן־ תְּפַלֵּ֑ס נָע֥וּ מַ֝עְגְּלֹתֶ֗יהָ לֹ֣א תֵדָֽע׃פ

passages.text: So now, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his sons.
He warns them about a dangerous woman.
He says, "My sons, listen to me."
He says, "Do not turn away from my words."
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ־ לִ֑י וְאַל־ תָּ֝ס֗וּרוּ מֵאִמְרֵי־ פִֽי׃

passages.text: Keep your path far from her; do not go near the door of her house, lest you concede your vigor to others, and your years to one who is cruel; lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich the house of a foreigner.
passages.sermon:
The woman in this passage is a seductress.
She leads people away from wisdom.
She does not consider the path of life.
Her ways are unstable.
She does not know it.
Keep your path far from her.
Do not go near the door of her house.
If you go near, you may give your strength to others.
You may give your years to someone who is cruel.
Strangers may take your wealth.
Your hard work may enrich the house of a foreigner.
passages.original: הַרְחֵ֣ק מֵעָלֶ֣יהָ דַרְכֶּ֑ךָ וְאַל־ תִּ֝קְרַ֗ב אֶל־ פֶּ֥תַח בֵּיתָֽהּ׃ פֶּן־ תִּתֵּ֣ן לַאֲחֵרִ֣ים הוֹדֶ֑ךָ וּ֝שְׁנֹתֶ֗יךָ לְאַכְזָרִֽי׃ פֶּֽן־ יִשְׂבְּע֣וּ זָרִ֣ים כֹּחֶ֑ךָ וַ֝עֲצָבֶ֗יךָ בְּבֵ֣ית נָכְרִֽי׃

passages.text: At the end of your life you will groan when your flesh and your body are spent, and you will say, “How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks to a person who ignored wisdom and discipline.
At the end of your life, you will groan.
Your body will be used up.
Your strength will be gone.
You will say, “I hated discipline.”
You will say, “My heart despised correction.”
passages.original: וְנָהַמְתָּ֥ בְאַחֲרִיתֶ֑ךָ בִּכְל֥וֹת בְּ֝שָׂרְךָ֗ וּשְׁאֵרֶֽךָ׃ וְֽאָמַרְתָּ֗ אֵ֭יךְ שָׂנֵ֣אתִי מוּסָ֑ר וְ֝תוֹכַ֗חַת נָאַ֥ץ לִבִּֽי׃

passages.text: I did not listen to the voice of my teachers or incline my ear to my mentors.
passages.sermon: I did not listen to my teachers.\r\nI did not pay attention to my mentors.
passages.original: וְֽלֹא־ שָׁ֭מַעְתִּי בְּק֣וֹל מוֹרָ֑י וְ֝לִֽמְלַמְּדַ֗י לֹא־ הִטִּ֥יתִי אָזְנִֽי׃

passages.text: I am on the brink of utter ruin in the midst of the whole assembly.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker stands before the whole assembly.
The speaker faces complete ruin.
The speaker is almost destroyed.
This happens in public, among many people.
passages.original: כִּ֭מְעַט הָיִ֣יתִי בְכָל־ רָ֑ע בְּת֖וֹךְ קָהָ֣ל וְעֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice about faithfulness in marriage.
It uses the image of water to teach this lesson.
Drink water from your own cistern.
Drink running water from your own well.
Do not seek satisfaction outside your own marriage.
Be faithful to your spouse.
passages.original: שְׁתֵה־ מַ֥יִם מִבּוֹרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝נֹזְלִ֗ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ בְּאֵרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Why should your springs flow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares?
passages.sermon:
The writer speaks to a man about his life and relationships.
He uses the image of springs and streams of water.
He asks a question.
He says, "Why should your springs flow in the streets?"
He also says, "Why should your streams of water run in the public squares?"
He warns against letting what is private become public.
He teaches that what belongs to you should not be shared with everyone.
passages.original: יָפ֣וּצוּ מַעְיְנֹתֶ֣יךָ ח֑וּצָה בָּ֝רְחֹב֗וֹת פַּלְגֵי־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.
passages.sermon:
This teaching speaks to a man about his own blessings and relationships.
Let your blessings belong to you alone.
Do not share them with strangers.
Keep what is yours for yourself.
Do not let outsiders take part in what belongs to you.
passages.original: יִֽהְיוּ־ לְךָ֥ לְבַדֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֖ין לְזָרִ֣ים אִתָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth: A loving doe, a graceful fawn— may her breasts satisfy you always; may you be captivated by her love forever.
passages.sermon:
God sees every person’s actions.
God examines all paths people take.
May God bless your source of life.
Rejoice in your wife.
She is the wife you married when you were young.
She is loving like a doe.
She is graceful like a fawn.
Let her breasts satisfy you at all times.
Let her love always fill you with delight.
Stay devoted to her love forever.
passages.original: יְהִֽי־ מְקוֹרְךָ֥ בָר֑וּךְ וּ֝שְׂמַ֗ח מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת נְעוּרֶֽךָ׃ אַיֶּ֥לֶת אֲהָבִ֗ים וְֽיַעֲלַ֫ת־ חֵ֥ן דַּ֭דֶּיהָ יְרַוֻּ֣ךָ בְכָל־ עֵ֑ת בְּ֝אַהֲבָתָ֗הּ תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Why be captivated, my son, by an adulteress, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
The father warns his son.
He says, “Do not be captivated by an adulteress.”
He says, “Do not embrace the bosom of a stranger.”
passages.original: וְלָ֤מָּה תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה בְנִ֣י בְזָרָ֑ה וּ֝תְחַבֵּ֗ק חֵ֣ק נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sees every man’s ways.
The LORD watches each person’s actions.
The LORD examines all the paths a man takes.
Nothing is hidden from the LORD’s eyes.
passages.original: כִּ֤י נֹ֨כַח׀ עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־ מַעְגְּלֹתָ֥יו מְפַלֵּֽס׃

passages.text: The iniquities of a wicked man entrap him; the cords of his sin entangle him.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man does evil things.
His own evil actions trap him.
His sins tie him up.
His wrongdoing holds him tightly.
passages.original: עַֽווֹנוֹתָ֗יו יִלְכְּדֻנ֥וֹ אֶת־ הָרָשָׁ֑ע וּבְחַבְלֵ֥י חַ֝טָּאת֗וֹ יִתָּמֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own great folly.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man lacks discipline.
He does not accept correction.
He dies because he refuses instruction.
His own great foolishness leads him astray.
He wanders off the right path because of his folly.
passages.original: ה֗וּא יָ֭מוּת בְּאֵ֣ין מוּסָ֑ר וּבְרֹ֖ב אִוַּלְתּ֣וֹ יִשְׁגֶּֽה׃פ
